spec.reason: cartservice is a single replica with 1.0 reach across all five flows, is shared by frontend and checkoutservice, and has a 128 Mi memory limit. A prior 110 MB run caused errors across all flows, guard abort, and a 41-second recovery, so this is a high-risk, shopper-visible test of OOM behavior.
spec.hypothesis: Allocating 110 MB inside cartservice will exhaust its available memory, trigger errors across the shop, and likely cause the safety guard to abort the fault; the service may need time to recover.

spec.reason: This adds a network fault class alongside the cartservice memory stress and planned paymentservice pod failure, while probing the checkout dependency without repeating the memory test.
spec.hypothesis: Adding 100 ms of latency to paymentservice traffic will slow checkout, but should not cause widespread errors or trigger the safety guard.

decisions.reason: The cartservice memory-stress run was aborted after error rate reached 55% (peak 100%); all five flows were affected, cartservice restarted, and recovery took 25 seconds. Add a distinct network-fault class before the planned paymentservice pod failure to broaden coverage; the validator confirms this experiment is within policy.

The paymentservice delay completed with no errors or guard breaches; checkout was the only affected flow and slowed 5.51× (peak p95 117.8 ms), while the prediction correctly anticipated its impact and slowdown but overpredicted errors. The remaining paymentservice pod_failure test probes a distinct failure class and the checkout dependency, complementing the memory_stress and network_delay runs.
